**Video:** [Lec 37 — SVM Formulation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aO3FTnrf2bQ)

## Learning goals

- Write the **hard-margin SVM** primal.
- Rephrase SVM as ERM with **hinge loss** + $\ell_2$ regularizer.
- Outline why we pass to a **dual** problem over Lagrange multipliers.

## Before this clicks

Constrained optimization: minimize $f(w)$ subject to inequalities $g_i(w)\ge 0$. Form a Lagrangian with multipliers $\mu_i\ge 0$, then use primal/dual / KKT. Labels $y_i\in\{-1,+1\}$.

---

## Main ideas

### 1. Hard-margin primal

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min_{w,b}\quad &\tfrac12\|w\|_2^{2}\\
\text{s.t.}\quad & y_i\big(w^\top x_i+b\big)\ge 1\quad\text{for all }i.
\end{aligned}
$$

English constraint: **no training point misclassified** (and all lie outside/on the margin slab under the $\pm 1$ scaling).

Note the swap vs vanilla ERM storytelling: objective focuses on parameters $\|w\|$; constraints mention **data**. The Lagrangian will mix them again.

### 2. Hinge loss + $\ell_2$ reading

SVM is ERM with linear hypotheses, **hinge** loss

$$
L\big(h(x),y\big)=\max\big(0,\,1-y\,h(x)\big),
$$

plus an $\ell_2$ penalty / constraint on $w$. Points with $y\,h(x)\ge 1$ pay zero hinge; violators pay linearly. Hard-margin assumes a separator with zero hinge everywhere exists.

### 3. Path to the dual

1. Form the Lagrangian of the primal (multipliers $\mu_i\ge 0$).
2. Minimize over $(w,b)$ to get the **dual function** $Q(\mu)$.
3. Maximize $Q(\mu)$ over $\mu$ (dual problem) with a standard QP solver.
4. Recover $w^\star$ (and $b^\star$) from $\mu^\star$.

Duality swaps roles: optimize multipliers, then reconstruct the primal weights. Next lecture builds $Q(\mu)$ explicitly.

---

## Worked mini-example

Hinge at a point with score $s=w^\top x+b$:

| $y s$ | hinge |
|------:|------:|
| $2$ | $0$ |
| $1$ | $0$ |
| $0.2$ | $0.8$ |
| $-1$ | $2$ |

Only points inside/wrong side of the margin contribute loss.

---

## Common confusions

| Confusion | Clarification |
|-----------|---------------|
| Hard-margin always exists | Only if data are linearly separable. |
| Hinge = 0–1 loss | Hinge is a **convex upper bound** surrogate of 0–1. |
| Dual is optional trivia | Practice solves the **dual QP**; primal $w$ is reconstructed. |
